title: Three-year extension for Storybrook West subdivision
subtitle: Special meeting called over a lapsing approval deadline; density target and late timing questioned by councillors.
overview: Council held a special meeting on October 8, 2024 for one reason: the draft plan approval for the Storybrook West subdivision (Plan 23T-16003) was due to lapse on October 9. Council supported a three-year extension {{vote:m1}}, and the resolution and staff report will go to the County of Wellington, the approval authority.

Staff explained that the lapsing condition requires a council resolution before the deadline. The extension had been expected to come forward with a servicing report tied to the planned Colborne Street reconstruction, but that report did not reach council in September. Staff only realized late the week before that the date fell before the next regular meeting. Without the extension, the developer would have had to reapply for draft approval, at considerable time and expense.

For residents, the decision keeps the large, multi-phase subdivision moving through its remaining phases. Councillors asked why the matter was so late and whether the density met county targets. Council also passed its confirming by-law and adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council supported a three-year extension of draft plan approval for Plan 23T-16003 and directed that the resolution and Staff Report PLN2024-37 be sent to the County of Wellington.

debate: Several councillors asked why the extension was not brought forward in September. Staff said it could have been, but it was expected to be included in a servicing agreement report that was delayed, and the October 9 lapse date was only noticed late the previous week.

One councillor asked why the matter had not been discussed earlier, given it was known an extension would be needed. Staff said an extension is not granted until needed, but it should have reached council sooner.

A councillor asked whether the phases meet the county's greenfield density target. Staff said the calculation rules have changed so the two are hard to compare and the target cannot be applied retroactively, but the result would be pretty close.
The developer's representative apologized for the inconvenience, said the matter was significant to the developer and the township, and agreed with the staff report.
